title: vault-meta — case shape (v0.1)
description: Pins one byte-level case for protocol::serialize_vault_meta + protocol::parse_vault_meta — the create-time MYV1 encoder/decoder pair (distinct from the landed vault_meta_rewrite which pins only the password-side rewrite path). Two case kinds: 'roundtrip' (input field-by-field → expected 345-byte blob, plus parse round-trip), 'parse_fail' (tampered blob → structural rejection via ProtocolError::InvalidVaultMeta). Spec contract: docs/spec/protocol.md §9.3.

vector_id.description: Stable identifier of the form 'vault-meta/v0.1/<descriptive-slug>'. Immutable once shipped.

oneOf.title: roundtrip — pin serialize_vault_meta byte output + parse round-trip

expected_vault_meta_hex.description: Full 345-byte serialized MYV1 blob (hex). Implementations call serialize_vault_meta with the reconstructed VaultMeta and compare byte-equal; round-trip property additionally requires parse_vault_meta(expected) to succeed without error.

oneOf.title: parse_fail — pin structural rejection of malformed MYV1 blob

input_blob_hex.description: Tampered or malformed blob bytes (hex). May have wrong magic, wrong protocol_version byte, non-zero reserved byte, malformed KDF params block, or short/long length.

expected_kind.description: Rust reference returns Err(ProtocolError::InvalidVaultMeta) — a single non-distinguishing variant per spec §6.4 closed-enum discipline. Ports MUST NOT distinguish which structural rule fired beyond 'this is not a valid vault.meta'.

informational_tamper_description.description: Human-readable note on which byte(s) were tampered with relative to the canonical roundtrip case (e.g., 'byte 0 (magic[0]) 0x4d → 0x4e' or 'byte 5 (reserved) 0x00 → 0x01'). Informational only — runner does not consume this field.
